text:
liam: heads up — observed steady memory growth on long streaming chat sessions when tool loops are active. repro script attached.

maya: hmm, is this the same KV residency drift from last month or a new pattern?

liam: different. last time it was big page allocations. this one looks like slot-level churn inside the KV slab. growth is linear with session length and number of loops.

ravi: can you drop the pprof diff and the command you used to repro?

liam: yes — ran load_test against local-runtime w/ tracing enabled.
Command: `python tools/load_test.py --host http://localhost:8080 --sessions 20 --session-length 1800 --tool-loop 40 --streaming true`
pprof heap delta snippet:
```
pprof: heap profile: 12.3MB increase
   6.4MB  52.0%  6.4MB  52.0%  runtime.malg
   3.2MB  26.0%  9.6MB  78.0%  github.com/redwood/runtime/kv.(*slot).alloc
   2.7MB  22.0% 12.3MB 100.0%  bytes.makeSlice
```

olivia: allocs inside kv.slot.alloc? that smells like small object churn. did you instrument slab reuse counters?

liam: yes — we added counters: slab_free_count drops slowly; slab_alloc_count ramps up steadily. eviction events occur but freed slots are fragmented (many <64B holes).

ravi: I ran a quick flamegraph of `kv.lookup -> slot.alloc -> bytes.makeSlice` and saw thousands of tiny allocations per second during tool callbacks. Tool outputs are small but frequent.

maya: could be caused by our recent change to PREFETCH_POLICY + batch_window_ms reduction. less batching -> more frequent KV writes and short-lived entries.

olivia: also check `KV_CACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD`. If eviction is too conservative we keep many small fragments around instead of coalescing.

liam: stack trace from sample:
```
runtime.mallocgc
github.com/redwood/runtime/kv.newSlot
github.com/redwood/runtime/kv.(*cache).insert
github.com/redwood/runtime/serving/handler.handleToolResult
``` 

ravi: interesting — `newSlot` is creating a separate []byte per tool result. We used to use a shared buffer pool; looks like the pool was disabled by the recent refactor to make copy-on-write safer.

maya: can you check mmap stats? if fragments are many small mmaps that'd be worse.

liam: not mmaps — allocations are from the heap. /proc/<pid>/smaps shows many RSS increases inside anon hugepages? but not full mmaps. Likely fragmentation inside the Go heap.

olivia: possible mitigation: re-enable pooled buffers for tool results and coalesce consecutive small writes into one slot when session is streaming. Also consider defragmentation pass on eviction.

ravi: I prototyped patch to reuse a sync.Pool for `[]byte` for slot payloads. Ran the same load test — RSS delta reduced by ~60% and slab_free_count recovered faster. blowing patch into a branch for review.

liam: awesome. can you add a flag to toggle `KV_COALESCE_SMALL_WRITES` so we can A/B compare on dedicated nodes?

ravi: will do. also adding histograms for per-slot lifetime and fragmentation-size to console metrics so we can correlate.

maya: action items:
- ravi: PR for pooled buffers + metric histograms (ETA today)
- liam: run long repro with coalesce toggle on/off and attach flamegraphs (ETA tomorrow)
- olivia: add short doc on eviction tuning knobs and suggested defaults for streaming-heavy workloads

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for runtime/kv-pool-reuse (sha: d4c3b2). :gear:

liam: thanks — will follow up with the long-run numbers. if this reduces slot churn we can avoid more invasive defrag work.

olivia: good plan. if the pool doesn't completely fix it we'll look at slab compaction or increasing min slot size to reduce fragmentation.

ravi: uploading initial heap + flamegraph to the thread — link: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/kv-slot-churn/1887654321

liam: saw that, thanks. quick note: repro uses tool-loop outputs of ~120B each; if someone else can try with 32B / 512B to map the slope that'd be helpful.

maya: i'll run the size sweep later today.

liam: thanks all :thumbsup:
